I know this may be worrying to hear, but acting quickly is the best thing you can do. The symptoms you've described are signs of acute pancreatitis, which means an inflamed pancreas. The pancreas is a small organ behind the stomach that helps with digestion and blood sugar control. When it becomes inflamed, it can be serious, and it is a recognised side effect of some medicines. Because of this, it needs urgent medical attention. Please do not wait.

The emergency team is there to help with exactly this kind of situation. They can assess you properly and give you the care you need, and getting seen promptly is the most reassuring step you can take.

If you think you may have taken too much medicine, you can also call the Poisons Information Centre on 13 11 26. The people there are used to helping with questions like this, and they can talk with you about what has happened.

**First, the important bit:** stomach pain and vomiting since last night need checking in with your clinician today, even if you think it's down to the injection. Nausea is common in the early stages, so feeling a bit queasy wouldn't be unusual. However, **persistent or severe stomach pain and vomiting aren't typical side effects**, and they could mean something else is going on. That's not meant to alarm you. It simply means a professional should take a look so you get the right answer. Please contact your doctor or the support team before your next dose.

**On the meal prep:** Yes, you can freeze cooked rice. It keeps well and thaws quickly, which makes it very convenient. That's a solid strategy for the week, and it's a sensible way to make sure you always have something ready to hand without much effort.

For variety without extra cooking, there are a few easy options. You can rotate your proteins (chicken, fish, lean mince, tofu), change your veggies week to week, and try different seasonings or sauces (soy, pesto, curry powder, lemon and herbs). Even the same base ingredients can feel like a completely different meal with a simple flavour swap, so you shouldn't get bored of your prepped food.

But let's get the stomach issue sorted first. Reach out to your clinician or support team today. They'll want to know what's happening, and they're there to help you with exactly this kind of thing. Once you've spoken to them, you can go back to focusing on your meal prep and your progress with a clearer mind.
